action.message:
I edited django/contrib/admin/options.py to fix ModelAdmin.lookup_allowed() incorrectly raising DisallowedModelAdminLookup when a foreign key is used as a primary key.

Root cause: the loop that builds `relation_parts` skipped a lookup part whenever the previous field was a relation and the current field was not among the previous relation's target fields. This was intended to collapse concrete-inheritance parent links (e.g. `employee__department__id` -> `employee__department_id`), but it also triggered for a OneToOneField used as a primary key, so `restaurant__place__country` was wrongly collapsed to `restaurant__country`, which is not in `list_filter`.

The fix adjusts the condition so the part is only skipped for genuine concrete-inheritance parent links (checking the relation's parent-link status) rather than for any relation whose target fields happen to include the field.

Verification: ran the scoped public regression selection (`modeladmin`), which passed — 162 tests, OK, returncode 0. Note that public regression success does not guarantee host feature acceptance, which the host runs separately.
